clue.text: Cricket ground is sad Ben got out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spectator called Ben is miserable because he has been dismissed at the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link between definition and wordplay; the fodder is just SADBENGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgbaston is the Test match venue in Birmingham, home of Warwickshire county cricket.

clue.text: Gripped object stupid European will break

indicators.note: these letters break into the other word, splitting it apart

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
gross can mean coarse and dull, stupid

explanation.surface: A foolish European is set to smash a thing that has caught his attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To be engrossed is to be absorbed in something, held fast by it.

clue.text: Belgian city described by Edinburgh entrepreneur

indicators.note: described as in drawn round, so the word sits within these two words

explanation.surface: A Scottish businessperson tells of a trip to a city in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghent is a major port and university city in the Flanders region of Belgium.

clue.text: Start working, returning extra suits chap oddly selected

indicators.note: returning means going back, so those letters are read in reverse
only the odd-numbered letters of these words are chosen

explanation.surface: A spare actor plays the part of a man in suits picked at random.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3, 5 and so on of EXTRA SUITS CHAP gives ETAUTCA; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate a machine is to set it in motion, to make it operate.

clue.text: Little change previously seen in Agatha Christie detective

definitions.meaning: first meaning: twopence, a small coin of pre-decimal British money
second meaning: ..., partner of Tommy in Christie's detective stories

explanation.surface: A small coin turns up in a whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' only links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppence was Britain's old twopenny coin, a trifling sum, and also the name of Christie's sleuth Prudence Cowley.

clue.text: Element symbolically occupying the centre of Winnipeg

definitions.text: Element symbolically occupying the centre of Winnipeg

parts.words: Element symbolically occupying the centre of Winnipeg
parts.note: the chemical symbol of this metal is Ni, the two middle letters of Winnipeg

explanation.walkthrough: WinNIpeg has the chemical symbol NI at its centre, and that symbol belongs to this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel is a silvery metallic chemical element, atomic number 28, whose symbol is Ni.

clue.text: Efficient computer with no frills

indicators.note: frills are trimmings at the edges, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a tablet is a handheld computer

explanation.surface: A description of a basic, stripped-down computer that still does the job well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able is capable and competent, a synonym for efficient in getting things done.

clue.text: Butterfly book, margin having rough notes

parts.note: a rim is an edge or margin

indicators.note: rough means roughly arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book about butterflies with jotted remarks scribbled in its margins.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a yellow butterfly common in Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Each journalist concealing scandal initially relieved

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so a letter sits within these

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Every reporter covering up a scandal ends up feeling better.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased pain or worry has been lessened, so eased is a synonym for relieved.

clue.text: Empty tin into large vessel

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Instructions to tip a tin's contents into a big container.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant room or seat is unoccupied, an adjective meaning containing nothing.

clue.text: Large jar picked up

indicators.note: picked up as a sound is heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to jar is to grate, to have a harsh irritating effect

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a big pot from a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a noun, a container, but it is the verb meaning to grate on the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is a straightforward synonym for big or of considerable size.

clue.text: Pig-like animals eat endlessly, attracting tooth decay

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to peck is to eat in small bites
caries is the dental term for tooth decay

explanation.surface: Animals that gorge themselves without stopping end up with rotten teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Peccaries are hoofed mammals of the Americas closely resembling wild pigs.

clue.text: Overhaul not to be considered before March

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: something out is out of the question, not to be considered
to march is to pace, step out

explanation.surface: An idea dismissed until some point ahead of the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month thanks to its capital, but it is the verb to pace; 'Overhaul' here means overtake, not repair.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a rival in a race is to catch and pass them, which is to go faster than them.

clue.text: Cutting speed unusually learner driver, American, went by

indicators.note: cutting into means these letters slice into the middle of the others
unusually signals that the letters are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver from America speeding oddly as they cut through traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns SPEED into EPSED; 'Cutting' puts L and A inside it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has passed, so the verb is a synonym for passed or went by.

clue.text: Judgement of one lacking in awareness

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: sentience is the capacity to feel and be aware
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A verdict on someone who seems oblivious to what is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the punishment a court pronounces, its judgement on the guilty.

clue.text: Supporting number Sue felt wrong for musical instrument

indicators.note: in a down answer the later piece is below and so supports the one on top
wrong means set out incorrectly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sue sang a backing number but felt she had got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' in a down clue means placed underneath: the anagram of SUE FELT goes beneath NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose flute is a wind instrument blown through the nostril, found in Polynesia and Asia.

clue.text: Unproductive time over for group of soldiers

indicators.note: over as in turned over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: poor soil or a poor season is unproductive

explanation.surface: A spell of idleness for a military unit comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of cavalry or armour, a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Close-fitting sweaters left individual covered in marks on skin

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped up within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: pocks are pockmarks, scars on the skin
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A lone person was left with a spotty complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo necks are jumpers with a high, close turned-over collar, known in America as turtlenecks.

clue.text: Mocking adult wearing cords in rambles

indicators.note: the wearer is inside the clothes, so this letter goes within
rambles means wanders about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up goes walking in the countryside dressed in corduroy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles' turns CORDS IN into SRDONIC, and the adult goes inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardonic remark is grimly derisive, scornful in a cynical way.

clue.text: Counter leader of opposition party

parts.note: a counter in a board game is a disc

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word

explanation.surface: A politician argues against the head of a rival political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' reads as a political party, but it is the definition: a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club evening with dancing to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Tackling debt lord is occasionally offensive

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so these letters wrap round the debt
occasionally means every other one, so alternate letters are used

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A nobleman dealing with money owed is sometimes rude.
explanation.walkthrough: An IOU is a note promising to repay; 'occasionally' here picks the second, fourth and sixth letters, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, causing strong dislike and offence.

clue.text: Spooner's put up with agony making bloomer

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with it; it sounds like bare
hell is a state of agony

explanation.surface: An instruction to endure suffering in order to produce something.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAR HELL with its starting sounds swapped gives HARE BELL; BEAR is spelt as its sound-alike BARE so that the swap spells the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and the harebell is a blue wild flower of grassland.

clue.text: Obscure phenomenon exciting astronomers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to hide or overshadow
second meaning: a solar or lunar event in which one body blocks another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to hide from view.
explanation.definitionFit: One body passing in front of another hides it, and that celestial event thrills sky-watchers.

clue.text: Condition of rope, perhaps strengthened to grip beam

definitions.note: an adjective describing the state a worn rope is in

indicators.note: to grip is to hold within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: fed as in nourished and so built up and strengthened
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A rope made stronger so that it can hold a wooden beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope that is frayed has worn, unravelling strands; 'perhaps' shows rope is only one example.

clue.text: Comparatively muscular male joins row over female

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a tier is a row of seats, one above another

explanation.surface: A man takes his place in a row ahead of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Heftier means bulkier or stronger, the comparative of a word describing a brawny build.

clue.text: Frequent trouble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to visit a place often
second meaning: to keep returning to disturb, as a ghost or worry does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' reads as an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular visitor haunts a pub, and painful memories haunt a person, distressing them.

clue.text: Brief suggestion by retired police officer for swimmer

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: PLOD is British slang for a police officer, after Mr Plod in the Noddy books

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A short tip offered by a former policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, a strong and fast swimmer.

clue.text: Points Frank detailed

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: frank means honest and open

explanation.surface: A man called Frank sets out the particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name thanks to the capital; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To point a blade is to give it a sharp tip, which is what a whetstone hones.

clue.text: South American a Nauru guy condemned

indicators.note: condemned suggests these words are wrecked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from the Pacific island of Nauru has been sentenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uruguayan is a person from Uruguay, a country in South America.

clue.text: Review of international nursing home brings alarm

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the whole is read backwards
nursing means holding something close, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cap is awarded for playing for one's country, so an international player is a cap
in means at home

explanation.surface: An inspection of an overseas care home causes worry.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a cap is awarded each time a player represents their country, so a cap means an international player; 'Review of' reverses the whole container, not just CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, which is what alarm means as a noun.

clue.text: Secured renewable energy supplier reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the tide drives tidal power, a renewable source

explanation.surface: News that a green power company has locked in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied is fastened with a knot or cord, made secure.

clue.text: Trim son does the ironing?

definitions.note: read as DE-CREASES, removes creases; the question mark flags the playful reading

parts.note: to trim is to cut back, decrease

explanation.surface: A parent tidies a son and then gets on with the household pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: ironing takes the creases out of clothes, so it de-creases them.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as de-creases, the verb means removes creases, which is just what pressing clothes with an iron achieves.
